reason: The iron-group core has lost fusion support, so gravity should drive its collapse.
expectation: The core will collapse into a denser state.

effect: The iron-group core is collapsing into neutron-rich matter; dense-matter pressure may now affect its collapse.
reaction: The conversion of protons and electrons into neutrons is a striking detail.
reason: Pressure in dense neutron-rich matter should act on the collapsing core.
expectation: The dense core will resist collapse, possibly producing a bounce.

effect: Dense-matter pressure produced a neutron star, completing the central-remnant goal. The enriched layers still need to be scattered.
reaction: The distinction between a neutron star and a more massive black-hole remnant is useful.
reason: The remaining onion of burning shells and flood of neutrinos seem the most plausible ingredients for the explosion, though I am guessing at the exact pairing.
expectation: Neutrinos will help drive an explosion that scatters the star’s enriched layers.

effect: The burning shells have no available combination, so the neutrino pairing does not work from that side.
reaction: That was unexpected; I need to check what can drive the explosion.
reason: Inspecting the neutrino flood should reveal its available role in scattering the layers.
expectation: It may identify a partner involved in the explosion.

effect: Neutrinos interacting with the collapsing core produced an outward shock, which may now scatter the stellar layers.
reaction: It is useful to see neutrino energy helping the shock overcome infalling material.
reason: The outward shock is the plausible mechanism for scattering the enriched burning shells.
expectation: The shock will eject the enriched layers into space.

effect: The shock scattered the enriched layers as expanding ejecta, completing the remaining goal while leaving a dense remnant.
reaction: Seeing the shock connect the core collapse to the scattered material was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Creating the outward shock was most worthwhile: it showed how neutrino energy can help a shock overcome infalling material in this modeled explosion.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to pair the shells directly with neutrinos was the least informative passage, though it prompted a useful inspection.

surprise.text: I expected neutrinos to act directly on the shells; instead, their available partner was the collapsing core.

arbitrary.text: The direct neutrino–shell pairing initially seemed plausible, so its rejection felt somewhat opaque until inspection revealed the core connection.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the enriched ejecta contribute to later world-making; the shock sequence made that progression interesting.
